nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: What insights does this research aim to offer for sustainability policies?
nodes.answer: The research aims to offer insights into how sustainability policies can be tailored to meet the needs of different populations and socioeconomic strata.
nodes.paragraph: Addressing socioeconomic disparities is essential for understanding environmental behavior, particularly in regions with pronounced inequality. Economic disparities weaken collective engagement by reducing national identification and shared responsibility (Baland et al., 2018; Ignatow, 2005). They also exacerbate educational line- qualities, limiting access to knowledge necessary for sustainable practices (Zreik, 2023). Additionally, financial constraints in less developed countries hinder prioritization of envi- ronmental concerns, reflecting the challenge of balancing economic needs with sustainabil- ity ( arko lu & Kentmen- in, 2015; Zreik, 2023). This study leverages data from over 60 countries spanning developed and developing economies to explore how socioeconomic factors such as income, education, and employ - ment status influence environmental perceptions and pro-environmental behaviors. The global scope of this analysis provides a unique opportunity to examine how these factors operate across diverse cultural, political, and economic contexts. By examining a wide array of demographic groups, this research offers insights into how sustainability policies can be tailored to meet the needs of different populations and socioeconomic strata. Fur - thermore, the findings from this study contribute to a growing body of literature that seeks to understand the intersection of economic development and environmental sustainability, offering both theoretical insights and practical implications for policymakers.
